articles.title: Why Director Robert Eggers Calls His Brutal New Horror Movie Werwulf the Darkest Film He Has Ever Made
articles.summary: Werwulf just might be drector Robert Eggers’ darkest film yet. So bleak and dark, in fact, that Eggers recalled “when Jarin Blaschke, my cinematographer, first read the script, he said, ‘Does this take place in Hell?’”
articles.body:
“It was after Nosferatu and I said, ‘What's the darkest thing I can write?’” filmmaker Robert Eggers recently told me about the genesis of his upcoming horror film, Werwulf . The film takes place in 13th century England and follows a farmer, simply called Man, who has been cursed to live as a werewolf.

“Werewolves [in medieval European folklore] were doing things that were so extreme and taboo and violent that the culture couldn't accept that they were human and so they called them werewolves,” Eggers said about the historical underpinnings of his film. “So I thought that this was going to be the right so-called creature to inhabit a very dark movie.”

Werwulf just might be Eggers’ darkest film yet. So bleak and dark, in fact, that Eggers recalled “when Jarin Blaschke, my cinematographer, first read the script, he said, ‘Does this take place in Hell?’” Eggers and Blaschke’s collaboration goes all the way back to the helmer's feature film directorial debut, 2015’s The Witch. They’ve since worked together on each of Eggers’ subsequent pictures ( The Lighthouse , The Northman , Nosferatu , and now, Werwulf).

“When I did more research about werewolf folklore, it's very different from what we've seen in cinema. I understood that this also gave me the opportunity to explore some things that I explored in The Witch and – for reasons of my own inexperience and talent at the time and also for reasons of budgetary limitations – couldn't quite do, and I got a chance to try it again [in Werwulf],” Eggers said.

“I think I've derided The Witch on many occasions but I am proud of the screenplay and the screenplay was good. And as Alfred Hitchcock said, the three things you need to make a great film are script, script, script, so I think that, for the people who really relate to The Witch, I think that that is why. And then The Lighthouse, I love The Lighthouse but there's barely a story. And The Northman's Hamlet and Nosferatu was Dracula and this is finally an original story with a driving narrative again.”

In this exclusive clip from Werwulf, which can be viewed via the player above , Aaron Taylor-Johnson’s Man has been drafted by the King’s wolf hunters to join them in pursuing the wolves that are killing the sheep pivotal to England’s wool trade , the country’s biggest economy. While on the hunt, the man has an eerie encounter with a wolf where, for lack of a better phrase, game recognizes game.

“Aaron is the only person who could have played this role. I wrote the role for him. He's a very handsome man in a traditionally masculine way; he can grow a huge beard [and] he also has a haunted quality to him, but he also has a dance background. So I knew that he would be capable of this incredible movement,” Eggers said. “And it was one of the things that excited me the most about what the werewolf transformations would be in this film, is that it is physically the actor doing most of it. Yes, David White, the special effects makeup designer, does more stuff after that, but I wanted it to be grounded in this body that is in agony.”

Taylor-Johnson worked for months with choreographer Marie-Gabrielle Rotie to perfect the movements required to portray the terror and pain of the werewolf transformations. The actor also took it upon himself to study wolves.

“I gave him a tremendous amount of research that I thought would be helpful, but it was something that I wasn't proposing that he wanted to do, [which] was to go to a wolf sanctuary and hang out with some real wolves,” Eggers recalled.

“It was one of the best things we did in prep also because it was something that I wasn't thinking of and it changed the film. It changed his physicality [and] the way that the alpha male wolf interacted with Marie-Gabrielle - she was there as well - influenced how Aaron's character interacts with Lily Rose [Depp], who plays his wife, physically. And then also the howl of the alpha male wolf being so close to him was really mind-blowing because, obviously, you have the high pitch mournful howl, but when you're a bit closer you also feel this subwoofer reverberating in my ribcage, not just the wolf's ribcage. It was really quite amazing. It was intimidating.”

Look for my full on-camera interview with Robert Eggers closer to when Werwulf opens in theaters December 25. Tickets to see Werwulf in 35mm are now available .

Jim Vejvoda (he/him) is IGN's Assoc. Director of Entertainment Content.

articles.title: Wizards of the Coast Sues Website That Prints Fake Magic: The Gathering Cards, Alleging Counterfeiting Operation
articles.summary: For as much as Magic: The Gathering has grown in popularity over the last several years, the market for proxies and counterfeits has also grown. And now, Wizards of the Coast is suing PrintMTG, alleging a counterfeiting ring for the trading card game.
articles.body:
For as much as Magic: The Gathering has grown in popularity over the last several years, the market for proxies and counterfeits has also grown. And now, Wizards of the Coast is suing PrintMTG, alleging a counterfeiting ring for the trading card game.

Wizards of the Coast filed the lawsuit (via Aftermath ) in its home state of Washington, alleging PrintMTG "operate as a complex and sophisticated network (...) engaged in trademark infringement, counterfeiting and criminal copyright infringement on a grand scale." Wizards seeks $28.65 million in damages.

For the most part, PrintMTG was a destination for people to print proxies, or essentially fake Magic cards that could stand in for real ones, for either playtesting or trying before you buy the actual card. And, thanks to the Reserved list, there are plenty of cards that cost thousands of dollars for a legitimate copy, so it's easy to see why going to a website and spending $0.75 on a proxy version instead was a popular choice.

Magic: The Gathering – Nauctis: The Sunken Realm New Cards

In its complaint, Wizards of the Coast seems to acknowledge the purpose that proxies serve, saying "an honest proxy is a stand-in for a real card that makes no claim to authenticity by appearance or otherwise. Though proxies are prohibited in all sanctioned Magic events, Wizards recognizes that private and noncommercial proxying is a vehicle players can use to further engage with the game, not to undermine it." But, it seems PrintMTG proxies were a bit too realistic.

Later on in the complaint, Wizards of the Coast describes what it sees as a legitimate proxy, which "include writing the name of a card in marker on a basic land card or on a blank card printed for this purpose, using one genuine card to represent another or sliding a slip of notebook paper into a card sleeve." PrintMTG and other proxy-printing websites like it, will instead print Magic's art on card stock, for a price.

Wizards of the Coast alleges that PrintMTG's proxies "directly harm Wizards by displacing sales of genuine cards" and damages "retail partners who sell those cards." But even beyond that, the company alleges that these counterfeits were "creating instability and uncertainty in the very secondary markets third-party retailers rely on as a revenue center."

There's a whole Reddit community that's sprung up, /r/RealOrNotTCG , where people post pictures of Magic cards to try and figure out if they're, well, real or not. However, PrintMTG is just one of many services that print realistic Magic proxies. This is a market that's been around for years, and it seems like Wizards of the Coast is finally cracking down on it.

This lawsuit comes after Wizards of the Coast recently changed the way booster packs work, and ahead of Darkhold Destiny, its third Marvel set.

articles.body:
The bulk of fans watching streams of GTA 6 are under 25 years old, according to recent stats compiled by StreamsCharts.

After 13 long years, GTA 6 is finally out in the wild. Rockstar’s highly anticipated release has already broken numerous records, one of the most impressive being that it became the single most popular game ever on both Twitch and Kick just 26 hours after its global release.

Now that it’s had a little time to breathe, more data is rolling in, including information about who’s watching streamers play the game. StreamsCharts , a data analytics company that studies games-focused streaming platforms, discovered that most viewers of GTA 6 broadcasts tend to trend under the age of 25.

According to Streamlabs’ stats, 30.8% of viewers in GTA 6 streams are 20 - 24 years old, making up the bulk of those watching the game across Kick, Twitch, and YouTube. (Painfully, StreamsCharts pointed out that these players were in elementary school when GTA 5 came out.) 16.8% of these viewers are 17 - 19, with 8.5% accounting for viewers 16 or under. The second-largest age range watching GTA 6 streams are viewers aged 25–29. 11.6% of viewers are 30–34, and the numbers keep dropping from there.

StreamsCharts also found that an overwhelming majority of these viewers are single men, accounting for 83.8% of the gender divide. That’s not to say that gals aren’t also watching streamers play Rockstar’s latest; 14% of viewers are female, and if you’ve been on social media lately, you’ve probably seen a fair few female players showing off their outfits for Jason and Lucia or the viral conversation about how it’s, oddly, comparable to a crime-focused version of The Sims.

Perhaps unsurprisingly, the United States makes up the bulk of GTA 6 viewership. Brazil isn’t far behind, coming in at 12.4% of the game’s total audience; Spain and Germany follow at 6.9% and 6.8%, respectively.

Certain games have also experienced a drop in viewership following GTA 6’s release. StreamsCharts found that GTA 5 had the sharpest drop-off on Twitch, followed by the platform’s Just Chatting category and World of Warcraft.

The GTA hype train is in full swing, and it’s making big bucks for Rockstar. The company reportedly made a staggering $3.79 billion from the game in just 24 hours, making it the single biggest entertainment launch in history. Internet provider Comcast even revealed that it experienced its highest-traffic day ever as players downloaded the game to their consoles, and PlayStation confirmed that GTA 6 was its biggest game launch in the company’s history.

Just getting started in GTA 6 or wondering what to do next? Check out the Official Grand Theft Auto 6 guide right here on IGN. If you're still getting your bearings, discover GTA's new systems with the Beginner's Guide - 67 Tips and Tricks , or get all the details on the first chapters with the Chapter 1 Guide and Tips , Chapter 2 Guide and Tips , and Chapter 3 Guide and Tips . If you're already driving all around Leonida and want to know everything there is to find and do, see the Leonida interactive map .

Virginia (she/her) is IGN’s News Editor. With ten years of experience reporting on games and entertainment, she’s got a storied background in the fighting game community, influencer news, and viral online trends. Find her on Twitter at @TheeMissGlaze .

The Silverbreaker Mace is a unique weapon in Crimson Desert 's Charting the Unknown DLC. This one-handed mace can be used by Oongka and Kliff, and its passive perks make it a great addition to your arsenal. Here's how to find the Silverbreaker Mace in Crimson Desert.

The Silverbreaker Mace can be obtained just minutes after setting sail for the first time in Charting the Unknown.

It's located on Auronui Island, the very first place the Greymanes establish a naval foothold in the DLC. You'll find it in a buried chest on the eastern island.

Make your way to the eastern island, then look for a group of palm trees with yellow and green leaves. The chest is buried beneath them.

Dig up the chest with a shovel to claim the Silverbreaker Mace. It has three empty Abyss Gear sockets, and its damage increases with consecutive attacks.

articles.summary: The Spotted Seal is a secret mount you can get in Crimson Desert's Charting the Unknown DLC. You can actually tame and ride the seals you find on Iliya
articles.body:
The Spotted Seal is a secret mount you can get in Crimson Desert 's Charting the Unknown DLC. You can actually tame and ride the seals you find on Iliya Island, but there are a few hoops to jump through first. Here's how to find and tame a seal mount in Crimson Desert.

Spotted Seals can be found all along the beaches of Iliya Island east of the Great Coral Reef. They hang out in groups and spend most of their time sleeping.

You can only tame a Spotted Seal once it's in the water. Find a group of seals, then try to chase them into the sea.

It's finicky, but you can always go find another group of seals if they get away. Once you get a seal into the water, you'll see the prompt to hold Square / X to ride them like any other aquatic mount.

To keep a Spotted Seal permanently , open your inventory while mounted and then feed it food to raise its trust to 100. Then, you can take it in and register it as a mount!

articles.title: Grand Theft Auto VI Review, Gameplay Impressions, Videos and Top Features
articles.summary: Grand Theft Auto VI from Rockstar Games overdelivers.
articles.body:
Grand Theft Auto VI from Rockstar Games overdelivers.

It's a stunning statement, really. Each GTA tends to hang around in the top half of greatest games of all time discussions. When Rockstar isn't making them, it's busy making all-time classics like Red Dead Redemption 2 or quieter generational hits like Bully, Max Payne and L.A. Noire.

Thirteen years since the last entry in the series, GTA 6 arrives and almost laughs off all-time expectations with a best-ever open world, a level of immersion that's hard to explain and a game so gigantic and filled with depth that it's no wonder the rest of the video games released this year fled the November calendar like a sinking ship. They might want to start thinking about 2027 as a whole, too.

New College Football Playoff rankings revealed

Returning to Vice City, expanded and modernized, has gone from the imagination to the screen in ways that might leave the imagination wanting.

GTA 6 is breathtaking in its depth. Yes, all the bells and whistles are here in a way that modern hardware will spend years attempting to fully realize. It's a stunner of a looker, but the real treat comes in the near-endless details.

Density of both crowds and traffic is a feat for the gaming space. Same story, especially, for nighttime in GTA 6. It sounds a little strange rolling off the tongue, but this feels like the first game to let nighttime actually be dark , letting the stunning lighting systems take over in ways we've never really seen before.

Those light systems can be manmade, like headlights or the afterglow of a city's neons in the clouds, or natural, like lightning storms from a dynamic weather system.

While the odder-by-the-day Internet wages frames-per-second debates, the rest of the world will enjoy the way GTA masters the little things with alarming frequency. Just little appreciable things like dents in a punching bag, the random arrays of personal items scattered in each NPC car to give it a unique feel, the overwhelming number of enterable buildings, it just goes on and on.

In many ways, GTA is just bragging its game design superiority. Characters will organically squeeze through tighter spaces. They'll dual-wield or single-wield weapons or do everyday things naturally with their off-hands.

And on the sound design front, yes, there is no equal in the voice-acting department when weighing the protagonists right on down to the lowest of random NPCs out in the world. The budget demands it and delivers.

But it goes far beyond that. Yes, the mind-boggling number of stations, songs, and sheer material on the radio is borderline overwhelming. But everything, from the phone to the minigames and beyond, makes even a stroll down a street an engrossing thing.

The world simply feels like it would exist and move on without the player, which is pretty much a first in gaming. And the more measured pace of the experience almost encourages players to act more lawful and sane instead of a sociopath, fitting in to the point of maybe even obeying red lights. It's fun in a way that is honestly pretty hard to explain, but makes the action-packed missions and the actual time for combat all the more impactful.

Generally speaking, combat is a weighty, thrilling experience that layers atop the tried-and-true GTA experience. Take gunplay. Bigger weapons straight-up blast off limbs now.

And when the fight is done? Money to be had, sure, but if a player likes a victim's sunglasses, well, they can pluck those off the body and keep moving, too.

Same story for simple brawls with melee weapons. It's a little more measured than just button mashing, but that works too. Grisly violence and damage, this game has.

How much has GTA evolved? Bank heists were story missions with specific beats and scripted moments. But banks outside of the story could hardly ever even be entered. Now? Once equipped with the proper gear, players can rob whatever bank they choose in whatever manner they see fit.

There are consequences, of course. Namely, the Wanted system. It's evolved in the best way possible here: Now, police can only act on the information they have. Players don't have immersion-breaking map feeds to watch while they flee anymore. But they do have eyeballs and ears to listen to the radio callouts. And they have creativity: Dipping into a new car, a new outfit, hiding, blending in, there are just so many ways to experiment with and enjoy the Wanted system now that it's an exclamation point for the entire game (and will make going back to the older Wanted systems in the series very rocky).

Those wondering how Rockstar's Red Dead Redemption 2 systems would translate to modern GTA gameplay can rest easy:

In loose terms, a player's vehicle functions as the horse might have for players in RDR2. It houses a stash of goodies, ranging from stolen items to outfit changes (for bank robberies, of course) to bigger weapons like rocket launchers. That goofy rocket-launcher-from-out-of-the-jeans-pockets stuff is a thing of the past and GTA is much better for it.

Now, there's more weight to decisions players must make on the fly. That doesn't mean pausing time to work a scroll wheel. It means decisions matter and everything is more lifelike.

Speaking of lifelike, this hits life simulation better than something like the Sims at points. Players can very much wake up and brew coffee for buffs, hit a couple missions, then go bar-hopping while playing pool or whatever, all while keeping an eye on things like hunger, how much fuel is in the gas tank and calorie counts that might encourage a little exercise. There are buses, trains and rideshare companies to use to get around the map while flicking through a phone that features a fully functioning internet.

All that aside, GTA 6 almost encourages save-scumming a bit. They know it's going to happen anyway, so why not? A separate save file might be a good idea before doing some wacky stuff because, after all, one of the best stories in gaming history boasts multiple endings where a player's actions can very much dictate how things land after the 60-plus hours of long journey.

Jason Duval and Lucia Caminos are the most authentic GTA protagonists to hit the series.

Jason is an army veteran with shades of mystery and Arthur Morgan, in a good way. Lucia, though, is the real triumph of GTA 6. She's a nuanced, confident character with a huge range of emotions and by far the most likable protagonist not just in the series, but arguably in gaming outright.

Both are less exaggerated caricatures like past protagonists and something more, well, normal. And normal means relatable. There are degrees of relatability, especially when going out for some fun crimes, but these two are a masterclass of relatable characters that make players care, and quickly.

Attempting to explain the scope of the story is a task. There's less "let's go get rich for reasons" and more everyday struggle as the duo bumbles their way into mistakes while trying to improve their situation. It's more Bonnie and Clyde on the run than anything, and all the unforgettable set pieces and side characters are there.

And that's just talking about the main story. This isn't a world of un-interactable backdrops or window dressing. There's a gaming console in the player's house with full games. The classic GTA minigames with surprising depth are all over the map. All that while digesting the thousands of hours of in-game media content on television, radio or otherwise.

This is, by far, the most immersive open world in the history of video games.

There are side areas and niches that could function as their own video games on their lonesome. The car culture throughout the map is a good example. In some ways, this might as well be Forza through some of the ways players can tweak engines and performance. Even the quality of the paint jobs varies from the local car joint on the block or the professional dealerships elsewhere.

Some might bemoan some of the more mundane missions. But ironically, it's the playerbase besieged by scrolling TikTok that has lost the plot here. GTA missions have always smartly broken up the pace with goofy (or not) bits that develop characters and create moments. Think, hitting some yoga with Michael De Santa, to stay very brief with the examples.

Those who would declare that there isn't as much satirization of the real world simply aren't paying enough attention, either. It's not as blunt and in a player's face this time. Instead, it's smoothly woven into handcrafted NPCs out in the world and the many layers of media, radio or otherwise, that don't go overboard while developing a superb (and sometimes uncomfortable) message.

We could spend eons writing about all of the side activities or the little encounters that create huge impressions. But it would feel, well, criminal, to spoil some of these things. Or any of it, really.

Yes, on the technical front, GTA 6 doesn't always run the best and those accustomed to higher frames will notice the 30 FPS or even below moments. But in the grand scheme of things, GTA 6 is such a compelling, unique experience that the little hiccups almost have their own charm and aren't immersion-breaking.

Grand Theft Auto VI is the peak of video games. This is it, and will be for a long time.

Who had GTA writing the most compelling protagonists and overall romance in the medium? Who could have confidently predicted that the broad themes of satirizing inequality, unfairness of the systems and life in today's America would be so easily accomplished in these absurd times?

Few. And that's to say nothing of the more measured, paced gameplay that borders on simulation. It's a standout in all facets that masters its small bits in ways games dedicated to those niches don't match.

Detractors will nitpick, but GTA 6 was never promised to implement all of the GTA Online craziness into its core experience. It's unabashedly GTA and better for it. GTA Online will arrive later.

Most of all, GTA 6 remained true to itself. It's so far beyond that we're past comparing it to other games and the conversation should shift to how it compares to all-time classics in other mediums. Only its sequel, perhaps in a decade or more, is the real threat to it at this point.

articles.title: Despite Some Nice Moments, The Rings of Power Season 3 Ends as a Set-Up for Future Seasons Rather Than Paying Off This One
articles.summary: While the final two episodes of The Rings of Power Season 3 have some exciting fan moments, they ultimately prove to be more about set-up than payoff.
articles.body:
Spoilers follow for The Rings of Power Season 3, Episodes 7-8.

The Lord of the Rings: The Rings of Power Season 3 finale, titled “The Doom of Men,” closes out a season that rejuvenated the flailing series with the promise that Sauron’s worst is yet to come in the just announced Season 4 . For a season that was all about the One Ring and the anticipation of an epic battle between good and evil, “The Doom of Men” ends with Sauron proving that guile remains his most potent weapon against his adversaries.

The season’s penultimate episode (“Orodruin”) saw Sauron finally succeed in forging the One Ring with the aid of the Balrog (voiced by Simon Pegg). While it was intriguing to see the devil make a deal with another devil, Pegg's voice was so manipulated that any ol’ actor could’ve played him. Episode 7 also saw Míriel turn down Elendil and go through with marrying Pharazôn, thus uniting the Númenóreans. Meanwhile, Durin and his family are banished from Khazad-dûm but make off with one of the rings given to the Dwarf-lords. That’s the last we’ll see of their storyline until next season as the Dwarves sat out the season finale.

“The Doom of Men” finally resolves the Gandalf/Dark Wizard storyline with Pallando sacrificing himself to save Gandalf in a classic Heel-Face Turn ending in redemptive death . Gandalf freed his old friend from the corrupting influence of the ring, which Pallando had apparently worn for all of an evening before Gandalf tricked him out of it. (Pallando wore the ring just long enough for the show to make an allusion to Gollum’s “my precious” line.)

While the wizards vs. Nazgnagôl battle felt awkwardly executed with all its obvious wire-work, at least it provided Gandalf and Pallando a few moments to finally fight side-by-side as allies. I’m not sure, though, if the Pallando storyline was ultimately worth taking up so much dramatic real estate over the last two seasons for such a brisk payoff. At the very least, Pallando’s death and the resulting liberation of his followers robbed Sauron of a good chunk of his army.

I enjoyed how Sauron tested Gandalf’s incorruptibility in a very Last Temptation of Christ manner, offering him the rule of Middle-earth if he’d just submit. I also liked Sauron’s short-lived ruse of conjuring a figment of Nori Brandyfoot (Markella Kavenagh in a cameo) in an attempt to dupe Gandalf, although I never believed that the show was bringing back Nori in any real way.

Elrond evoking his brother to help instill some hope in the Númenórean soldiers on the eve of their likely deaths was a nice touch. Despite a moment where he allows himself to ask the advice of Galadriel and Celeborn – whose relationship woes I haven’t found particularly interesting thus far – Pharazôn’s hubris ultimately gets the better of him. The Elves foresee the Doom of Men when Sauron surrenders so I fully expect Season 4 to end with The Fall of Númenor.

Jim Vejvoda (he/him) is IGN's Assoc. Director of Entertainment Content.

articles.title: Fresh Evidence Walkthrough - GTA 6 Guide - IGN
articles.summary: Dre’Quan finally met with top promoter, Royce Jones, during Grand Theft Auto VI’s Watch It mission, but he refuses to help with the Real Dimez
articles.body:
Dre’Quan finally met with top promoter, Royce Jones, during Grand Theft Auto VI ’s Watch It mission, but he refuses to help with the Real Dimez unless some personal business is handled first. This official IGN GTA 6 guide walks you through the Fresh Evidence main mission, including all choices and outcomes.

Having made a deal with Royce Jones, meet Dre’Quan at the Jack of Hearts before breaking into Dante’s mansion.

After meeting with Royce Jones at the Doigt d’Or hotel, Jason waits for a call from Dre’Quan for next steps. When he gets in contact, the plan is finally put in motion: they need to break into Dante’s mansion on Starfish Island and destroy the evidence he has on Royce.

But first, Jason is to meet him at the Jack of Hearts in the Crosstown area of Vice City.

Head inside and go through the club, up the stairs, and into the back office. Dre’Quan is chilling with some friends; hold L2 / LT and press Cross / A to have Jason ask if he’s ready. If you don’t ask, he eventually gets up anyway.

Follow Dre’Quan outside to his car and get in. The GPS automatically directs you to Starfish Island. Drive there.

As you approach, security recognizes Jason. He bluffs and tells the guard that they’re on a job for the Navarros. They’re allowed in and they pull up to Dante’s mansion, get changed into something less conspicuous, and wait until nightfall.

Dante leaves, and Dre’Quan asks Jason to leave his guns behind before they break in. They definitely won’t need them…

Despite Dre’Quan asking Jason to go over the wall to enter the mansion, you don’t have to. Feel free to enter however you’d like. If you do decide to go over the wall, just jump over it and ignore his attempt to give a leg-up.

Once inside the yard, wait for Dre’Quan to jump over. Then you need to find a way inside. Again, there’s no single way to do so. Just be careful because there are security guards prowling around outside and they attack if they see you.

After climbing over the wall, I entered the mansion by using the Snap Gun on the doors to the right of the garage.

When you enter the mansion, you’re prompted to find the bedroom. Be careful, though, as there’s a tiger prowling around the house.

If you climbed the wall, the tiger is definitely upstairs – be quiet to avoid it spotting you as it walks past to the balcony. If you entered another way, its placement may differ.

If the tiger does see you, it can kill you pretty fast.

The bedroom is located at the end of the upstairs hallway, just left of the “PARDON MY STYLE” poster.

Go inside. You need to find the key card to the elevator. It’s inside the bedside table drawer on the left side of the bed.

Turn to head back to the elevator and as you do, the tiger blocks your path here if you jumped the wall.

Follow Dre’Quan outside and jump over the railing to the floor below.

You land by the pool. There are two security guards here. Sneak around the pool towards them, and they walk away when you get close. Phew.

Go back into the mansion. The tiger has moved – it’s now on the ground floor behind the couches, exactly where you need to go.

Follow Dre’Quan into the kitchen area. You need to find something to distract the tiger. He suggests using meat from the fridge, but there’s also a bottle you can throw on the kitchen island, and a knife on the counter.

It doesn’t matter what you throw; the outcome is the same. The tiger moves out of the way to check out whatever was thrown, and you rush to the elevator with Dre’Quan.

The tiger spots them, but it’s too late – they’re already in the process of going down to the basement.

You exit out of the elevator into a…weird room. You need to find the surveillance room. Walk forward and look to your left for a “THE UNTOUCHABLE” poster.

Go into the room to the left, where there’s an interesting mural.

There’s a hole that needs a certain body part as a “key” – they thankfully do NOT need to do that, though. One of the colored objects on the shelf to the left is needed, though neither of them want to touch one. Understandable.

Dre’Quan suggests playing rock, paper, scissors to hash out who’s going to do it. Highlight him with L2 / LT and you get the following options:

If you don’t select in time, Jason automatically picks rock. No matter what you choose, Jason always loses, so pick whichever one. Poor Jason.

You can’t just grab any object from the shelf; you need to solve the puzzle. Look on the mural – there are several different symbols. Each object on the shelf has a symbol on the bottom.

It’s on the far-right side of the shelf; the metallic blue one.

Insert the correct object into the hole, then use D-pad Left and D-pad Right on the D-Pad to turn it like a key. A secret door unlocks. Enter the surveillance room.

Dre’Quan goes straight to the PC and starts copying evidence. While it’s copying, press Triangle / Y to watch as he browses through videos.

Suddenly, armored security shows up – the room has a silent alarm. Grab at least one gun from the wall. There are options on both sides of the room.

There’s no “best” option here in terms of which gun(s) to take from the wall; it’s entirely your preference. I personally recommend grabbing two – a close-range and longer-range one. This helps you take out guards at varying distances. I grabbed an AR and a shotgun.

Follow Dre’Quan back into the main basement room, where two security guards are. Take them out, then walk toward the elevator. It opens and one more guy bursts out.

Get inside the elevator and take it up to the main floor. Watch out – a guard is right there when the door opens.

You’re prompted to leave on Dante’s speedboat, which is parked at the dock to the west of the mansion, but you don’t need to – escape on foot or via vehicle if you want.

Note that no matter how you choose to leave the area, you do get a 3-Star Wanted Level and you need to lose the cops!

If you do leave on Dante’s speedboat, get in and hotwire it with the right thumbstick. The police chase you by boat and you need to clear the heat.

Once you’ve successfully escaped, it fast forwards to the next day. Jason and Dre’Quan meet with Royce’s personal assistant to give her the tapes. She gives them a sign-on bonus – Royce is very happy.

Dre’Quan gives Jason his share, netting you a sweet $10,000 reward. The mission ends.

articles.title: Headliners Walkthrough - GTA 6 Guide - IGN
articles.summary: Dre’Quan has finally made a breakthrough in promoting the Real Dimez, following the success of Grand Theft Auto VI’s Fresh Evidence mission. He
articles.body:
Dre’Quan has finally made a breakthrough in promoting the Real Dimez, following the success of Grand Theft Auto VI’s Fresh Evidence missio n. He needs Jason and Lucia’s help once more, this time preparing for the launch party set up by Royce Jones. This official IGN GTA 6 guide walks you through the Headliners main mission, including all choices and outcomes.

Dre'Quan needs a hand preparing for the Real Dimez' launch party. Meet him at Club VYB.

While Lucia waits for a call from Nate to say that the airport heist is a-go, Dre'Quan requests help with the Real Dimez' launch party. Go to Doigt d'Or on the east side of Vice Beach to begin the mission. Club VYB is inside.

Enter the club and walk to the back to find Dre'Quan. He’s sitting down talking on the phone. When he notices your character, he hangs up, greets them, and walks away – follow him to the main club room.

Royce is here. He greets him, then continues through. If you came alone, your partner shows up at this point. Keep following Dre'Quan and eventually, you reach a back office where the Real Dimez are.

The DJ is asking for help setting up, and Dre'Quan volunteered Lucia. You switch to her if you weren’t controlling her already and she follows the Real Dimez out of the room to the stage for sound checks.

When you gain control at the DJ booth, you are presented with three options to decide how the stage looks during the preshow later on in the mission, though only the color modification you choose stays. Feel free to design the stage however you like.

Rotate Pillars ( D-pad Left and D-pad Right on the D-pad) – Moves the four pillars surrounding the stage.

Move Pyramid ( Left Stick ) – Moves the pyramid on the ceiling.

Colors ( Right Stick ) – Changes the stage color. The color you choose carries over to the preshow.

After a few seconds, another option pops up: Effects. Hold L2 / LT and press the following buttons to test effects (you also get some funny dialogue from the Real Dimez depending on your button presses):

The night progresses and you switch to Jason, who is working security on the door. There are five VIPs requesting entry – you can only let three in . Dre'Quan says to pick big names and big spenders.

Who you pick affects the revenue and number of impressions the club receives. You also get a different cutscene, depending on who you choose to let in, and you see them throughout the night.

Game Developer Offer: $50,000 Followers: 5,282

Donatello Lambrini Offer: $0 Followers: 60,839,593

Jimmy De Santa Offer: $35,000 Followers: 55,275

You can see the total value of your three selections in the top right corner of the screen. Once you’ve picked your three VIPs, hold Circle / B to confirm your choices .

When choosing which VIPs to let in, don’t just look at their monetary offer – their social media followers matter, too. Impressions also helps the club which, in turn, affects your payout at the end of the night.

In your decision, measure the VIPs’ offers against their social media followers. For example, Donatello offers nothing yet has almost 61 million followers; the impressions here are probably worth the risk.

We went with Donatello Lambrini , Game Developer , and Jimmy De Santa (an Easter Egg for GTA 5 fans!) for a total of $85,000 and 60,900,150 impressions .//

The pre-show begins and you switch to Lucia. The VIPs are at their tables and are requesting special treatment, starting with Maleek Rivers, a football player. Follow the marker to his table.

Hold L2 / LT and press Cross / A to talk to him. He asks Lucia to change the lights to make him more visible. You have two choices:

Change Lights ( Cross / A ) – The DJ shouts out Maleek and his table gets extra spotlights shone onto it. He’s impressed.

Refuse ( Square / X ) – He is disappointed. He posts that he’s having a good time on Snapmatic either way.

Next, Dre'Quan asks Lucia to check on another VIP. Who this is depends on who you chose to let in as Jason, and it goes in the priority order listed below if you chose more than one of them. For example, if you picked Jimmy and the VIP, the objective will always be Jimmy's. If you chose the VIP and KD, the objective will always be the VIP's.

If you let Jimmy in, he has a request: invite a group of girls to his booth. You have two options:

If you deny the request , Jimmy is disappointed.

If you accept Jimmy's request , Lucia needs to approach the girls, who are located at the top of some stairs. Press Right Stick Click to pan your camera over to them.

Approach the girls from behind and hold L2 / LT and press Cross/A to have Lucia call out to them. She invites them over to Jimmy’s booth. They ask what he does for a living. Again, you have two choices:

It doesn’t matter what you choose, they’re impressed either way and go over.

If you let the VIP in (and didn’t let Jimmy in, too), he gets in an argument with another table about who has the most money, with them both causing chaos and wasting copious amounts of expensive alcohol.

You can Defuse the VIP’s table ( Cross / A ), go over to the other table and Defuse ( Cross / A ) or Kick Out ( Square / X ), or ignore the commotion completely – they calm down eventually anyway.

If you let KD in (and didn’t let Jimmy or the VIP in, too) – the promoter who accidentally got Dre'Quan kidnapped during the Photo/Shoot main mission – he has a request for Lucia. He asks if she can take a photo of everyone at his booth.

If you deny the request, he’s disappointed.

If you accept , KD hands Lucia his phone. You can zoom with D-pad Up and D-pad Down on the D-pad and turn the light on and off with L1 / LB , if you’d like, then press R2 / RT to take the photo.

After taking care of the two VIPs, regardless of whether you satisfied their requests or not, you switch to Jason. Dre’Quan needs him to escort a special guest inside the club. Before he can, though, a man approaches, begging to be let in. You have two choices here:

If you let him in , it increases the revenue the club makes for the night , therefore increasing your cut of the profits.

If you refuse, he leaves, annoyed. You can also walk past and ignore him completely and he leaves.

Proceed forward through the lobby and out through the main doors, where Dre'Quan is waiting. A car pulls up; approach and press Triangle / Y to open the door. It’s Sexyy Red , Dre'Quan's special guest. She greets D and they walk inside. Follow them through to the main club room.

When they arrive, Dre’Quan steps out to make a call, leaving Jason to escort Sexyy Red to the dancefloor. Walk down the stairs onto the floor, into the roped off area indicated by the pink marker.

The DJ announces Sexyy’s arrival and she begins dancing . She invites Jason to dance with her . You have two choices:

If you accept the invitation , hold R2 / RT to dance. You can press Triangle / Y to add some flourish, if you’d like. If you want to stop, press Triangle / Y to end it, otherwise just wait for the dance sequence to finish.

Lucia texts, asking Jason what he’s doing. You won’t lose any relationship points , so don’t worry – she’s joking.

If you decline , Sexyy asks Jason to grab her and her friends some drinks. Walk over to the bar, which is to the right. Highlight the bartender with L2 / LT and press Square / X to ask for VIP Service. Then return to Sexyy.

At this point, Sexyy complains she’s too far back – she wants a VIP booth. There aren’t enough to go around, though, meaning someone needs to go. There are four VIP booths, one of which is Maleek Rivers, the football player who asked Lucia for more lights. You can’t kick him out, but you can talk to him for some optional dialogue.

When you’ve decided which VIP to remove from their booth, highlight them with L2 / LT and select Move Out with Cross / A .

Jason upgrades your selected VIP to a balcony booth. Don’t worry - this doesn’t cut into your revenue from the night, it only impacts where Sexyy Red sits.

Once you free up a booth, you switch to Lucia. She’s in the green room with Jason and the Real Dimez as they get ready for their performance. Dre’Quan tells them to find a spot to watch the show from – they don’t want to miss it. Follow Jason back out onto the main floor, on the upper level this time. As they watch the crowd below, DWNPLY rushes in and storms the DJ booth and the stage with his goons, all armed to the teeth. He's back to try steal the Dimez' spotlight.

As he raps, Jason notices Dre’Quan is being held up by a thug named Bush. Lucia rushes over to stop DWNPLY. Approach the stage and press Triangle / Y to grab DWNPLY as he reaches out to a fan.

Pull him down from the stage, but as you do, you're tackled by one of DWNPLY's friends. He uses a baseball bat to try and choke Lucia out. Mash Square / X to throw him off as DWNPLY runs away. More thugs attack. Fight them off with the baseball bat.

Once they’re all down, you switch back to Jason who is rushing over to help Dre'Quan. Bush throws Dre'Quan to the floor. Be careful in this fight. Bush is armed with brass knuckles!

Press Cross / A right as Bush attacks to parry, then quickly press Square / X to counterattack. Hold Cross / A to block.

If you last long enough, Bush grabs Jason and attempts to smash the window and throw him out. Mash Square / X to escape his grip and continue the fight.

Eventually, Bush tackles Jason and slams him down against a countertop, hard. Mash Square / X again, then press Triangle / Y to grab a nearby knife; stab Bush with it.

They fall to the floor, and Jason pulls his brass knuckles off, putting them on himself. You can continue to punch Bush with the brass knuckles until Dre'Quan stops Jason – if you do, you get a Violent temperament bump, which contributes to your Criminal Profile in a negative way.

If you choose not to punch Bush with the knuckles on, Jason drops them. You get a Restrained temperament bump. Again, this contributes to your Criminal Profile, though positively instead.

You switch to Lucia. She rushes over to the back room where the Real Dimez are to check they’re okay. DWNPLY bursts in and holds them up at gunpoint when they reject him. He forces everyone into a corner, before pausing to fix his gun, which has jammed. While he struggles, you have two choices: disarm DWNPLY or wait .

If you attack DWNPLY while he is distracted, Lucia disarms and knocks him out.

If you wait , he ends up shooting himself in the foot.

With DWNPLY and his goons taken care of, the Real Dimez finally head out on stage. They perform the dirty or clean version of their song, depending on which option you chose during the Dealer’s Choice main mission back in Chapter 3 . After the cutscene, you’re Jason once more, dancing to the music with Lucia. Hold R2 / RT to dance, if you’d like, or press Right Stick Click to watch the performance (press again to go back to dancing).

Eventually, their performance ends and they leave the stage. You get one last choice here:

If you decide to stay , you Jason and Lucia get a relationship boost. There are some extra interactions you can do, too, though none affect anything.

Speak with your partner, Dre’Quan, and Wax for additional dialogue.

Speak with Sexyy Red, Maleek, and your chosen VIPs for additional dialogue.

When you’re ready to leave, follow the marker to Dre’Quan, who is chatting with Royce upstairs. Things are finally falling into place for Jason and Lucia's longtime friend.

A scene fast forwards to Jason, Lucia, and Dre'Quan walking on the beach (if you leave the club, it skips to this cutscene). They chat, and Jason tells Dre'Quan that they won’t be around as much anymore; they’ve got their own stuff to deal with. Then, it’s the next morning. Lucia and Jason are in bed. Her phone goes off, waking them up. It’s Nate: the job is on. She calls Raul, who asks them to meet at the planning room. Doing so starts the VCIA Takedown main mission .

Dre’Quan sends over your payment from the club night via BuckMe, which varies depending on your decisions from the mission .

articles.title: Yes, There Was One Thing Cut from GTA 6 for Australia, NZ
articles.summary: Rockstar chopped out a temporary stat buff from GTA 6, although players down under may not ever really notice it.
articles.body:
The Australian version of Grand Theft Auto 6 does differ from the international version in one small way; players down under are not able to use cocaine from their personal inventory to briefly overpower their stamina bar. NZ reportedly has the same version.

In GTA 6, baggies of cocaine can be collected (or skimmed from full bricks) and show up as a consumable on the item wheel in the same section as cigarettes, cigars, and joints. Using one triggers a buff that puts stamina in an overpowered state, albeit only for about 30 seconds. This function was never included in the Australian-specific version of the game, as it would have prevented GTA 6 from being classified in the country until it was removed. Australia’s classification laws allow illicit drug use in games, but using them can’t provide the player with gameplay benefits.

Overpowering your stamina (and everything else) is still possible via the use of adrenaline in the Australian version of GTA 6, and it’s also still possible to drink and smoke whenever you want. The general use of cocaine in story moments also still remains in the Australian version of GTA 6, because these instances aren’t associated with any in-game buffs.

While the caveat that forbids rewards for illicit drug use is bespoke to Australia – and doesn’t apply to NZ – NZ’s rating system (which does piggyback on some Australian and UK classification decisions for unrestricted content ) has its own idiosyncrasies. These recently caught out IllFonic’s recent Halloween multiplayer game , which was refused classification in Australia for illicit drug use linked to an incentive or reward (that is, that use of the drug provides a gameplay advantage to the player). Halloween since made its way to NZ, but not Australia. Since this is not Rockstar’s first rodeo, it knew exactly the tweak GTA 6 would require to skirt this continuing quirk in Australian video game ratings and avoid multiple submissions.

GTA 6 arrived late last week, crushing records and becoming the biggest entertainment launch of all time, with retail sales soaring to $3.79 billion in its first 24 hours. In my review for IGN I called it “the single most impressive video game I have ever played,” a sentiment shared by developers similarly stunned by how radically advanced it is.

Just getting started in GTA 6, or wondering what to do next? You can get stuck into the Official Grand Theft Auto 6 guide right here on IGN, consult our Beginner's Guide or Leonida interactive map , or get an idea of all the incredible flourishes to keep an eye out for by checking out our look at 99 incredible details you can find in GTA 6.

Luke Reilly is an award-winning journalist with 23 years of media experience. He previously served as Editor of Official PlayStation Magazine – Australia and Australian 360, before joining IGN in 2011. You can find him on Bluesky @mrlukereilly to ask him things about stuff.

articles.title: Child's Play Walkthrough - GTA 6 Guide - IGN
articles.summary: At the end of Grand Theft Auto VI’s Adventures in Babysitting mission, Andrés’ son, Rafa, is kidnapped by criminals. Abe urges Jason and
articles.body:
At the end of Grand Theft Auto VI ’s Adventures in Babysitting mission, Andrés’ son, Rafa, is kidnapped by criminals. Abe urges Jason and Lucia to get him back, otherwise he’ll drop their case for getting Tomás back. This official IGN GTA 6 guide walks you through the Child’s Play main mission.

Meet the Navarros at the Megamundo HQ and deal with Rafa’s kidnappers.

If You Don’t Start the Mission Immediately

If you don’t start the mission immediately after it becomes available, you’re urged to do so as time passes. First, Andrés texts Lucia to ask where you are. Later, Lucia texts Jason, worried that they’re taking too long.

Despite appearing as a timed mission, you can take however long you want to complete it – though be warned, you’ll lose some Criminal Profile points if you take too much time.

When you’re ready to get Rafa back, head on over to Megamundo HQ.

When you arrive, go inside the building. Gustavo, head of the Navarros’ security team, greets you and takes you upstairs to César’s office; the family is about to receive a hostage negotiation call.

The criminals want $25 million in exchange for Rafa. César refuses, offering only $3 million – they’ll only get a finger back for that. He “relents” and the trade location is set: a cement factory south of the airport.

There’s a major problem, though, and Jason steps in to offer help. He and Lucia will find a way to get Rafa back without anyone having to pay a cent.

Andrés, Jason, and Lucia head on over. You’re given control of the car as Jason; it’s a 1.58 mile drive away and the GPS directs you there. Along the way, Andrés calls Petra to confirm Rafa’s birthday, which they need as a code word when they arrive. Of course he doesn’t know…

When you reach the cement factory, Jason pulls up automatically. Security asks for Rafa’s birthday, Andrés answers, and they’re let in. Drive forward.

Lucia tells Jason to stop. Do so and she points out a tower; you can look at it with Right Stick Click / Right Stick Click if you want. She gets out and Jason and Andrés continue on to meet with the FAP kidnappers.

Gustavo is already there and offers to do the talking. Andrés refuses, but he won’t do any deals before he finds out if his son is okay. The criminals put him on the radio – he’s safe.

You switch to Lucia, who is atop the tower she pointed out to Jason. Hold R2 to look through the binoculars; you need to find Rafa. Use D-pad Up and D-pad Down on the D-Pad to zoom in if needed. He’s with a guard on the second floor of the factory.

From here, you’re given free reign to rescue Rafa. You can either do it stealthily or take the loud approach – it’s up to you. Note that if you do rush in guns first or you’re discovered, you miss a scene, showing the deal going down. It doesn’t matter, though – the overall outcome is the same.

Below, I’ll list my stealth route if you need more guidance. If not, click here to skip to the Escaping With Rafa section , after you successfully locate Rafa.

Here’s the silent route I took to find Rafa, starting at the top of the tower:

Climb (or slide) down the ladder. When you reach the bottom of the tower, Lucia automatically crouches near some stone blockades. There’s a lone FAP guard here; sneak behind him and press R2 / RT to grab him, then mash Square / X to take him out silently.

They drop a knife, which can be incredibly useful for silent takedowns. Grab it if you’d like.

Rush across the road to more barricades – yellow this time. There are multiple thugs here.

There’s a bottle on the right side, at the end of one of the barricades. I threw it at the cement truck ahead, which sets off the vehicle’s alarm. With the nearby men successfully distracted, run on past quickly. I went to the right, around the side of a big truck.

More guards are ahead. Wait and they should move out of the way and into a car, giving you an opening to go up the stairs ahead of you once they leave.

There’s a man up here; quietly take him down. He’s overlooking a big area, so him down means one less pair of eyes.

With the coast clear, hop over the railing toward the yellow forklift ahead and through the opening.

There are stairs here, but before moving on, use Focus Mode to highlight a nearby enemy. He’s keeping watch, so you need to take him out.

Hop over the railing to the right and stealthily take him down. Then go up the stairs.

At the top, take the ladder up. Be very quick as enemies may spot the downed man and be on higher alert.

There may also be a man that can spot you as you climb the ladder. If he does, he follows you up the ladder; wait at the top and quickly take him down before he can alert anyone else. You get off onto a large platform. Head left and go up the stairs.

At the top, look left to spot more stairs, heading down this time. Wait a moment as two patrolling men are walking here.

Use Focus Mode to track their movements, staying out of sight. Then rush down the stairs before they can spot you.

There’s a man up ahead, at the top of more stairs. Sneak very slowly behind him and take him out.

Turn around and go right from the stairs you just took.

At the end of the walkway, turn left around the corner and use Focus Mode to spot two more guards.

Don’t worry, though – as you approach them, Rafa screams and they get annoyed and move out of the way.

Go into the door to the left. Rafa is here, but so is a guard at a PC. Sneak up behind him and quickly take him out.

When you find Rafa, he’s playing a game and doesn’t understand the urgency of getting the hell out of dodge – typical iPad kid.

If you used the stealth approach to find Rafa, you switch to Jason. The thugs have run out of patience, but he has a happy update for Andrés – Lucia has Rafa. They need to find an exit.

Andrés makes an excuse about the wire transfer taking a long time. The kidnappers are NOT happy and draw their weapons. A shootout begins.

Shoot the thugs, using the nearby vehicles and shipping containers as cover if needed. Eventually, you are prompted to switch to Lucia – do so by holding D-pad Right on the D-Pad and pressing R1 / RB .

As Lucia, you need to successfully get Rafa out of there without either of them dying. There’s no stealth approach here – use the full force of your weapons to escape.

Send Rafa down the ladder at the end of the walkway, then follow suit when the coast is clear of shooters.

There are more enemies at the bottom. Take them up, then pick up the cowering yet somehow defiant Rafa. You’d think he’d want to get out of there. As soon as Lucia grabs him, a shooter drops down from the ladder you just descended – quickly take him out.

There’s another ladder ahead of you. Take it down – Lucia won’t send him down first this time. Hold Circle / B to slide down faster.

At the bottom, two thugs rush and grab Rafa before tackling Lucia. Quickly mash Square / X when prompted and she throws the man off.

You enter Combat Focus as she aims her gun at the other enemy. Shoot him.

More goons appear. Start taking them down…but Rafa has it handled, it seems. He rushes over to a nearby forklift and runs them over with it – hell yeah.

Protect Rafa from more criminals, then he climbs out and onto a nearby platform to take cover. Follow him.

As you reach him, more enemies appear. Shoot them until Jason, Andrés, and Gustavo appear in two cars, then pick up Rafa.

Carry him over to Gustavo’s car, where he is waiting, taking any remaining thugs out as you go.

Rafa climbs into the back seat, then Gustavo knocks Lucia down and drives away. Uh oh – there’s the rat.

You switch to Jason as he and Andrés are in hot pursuit. Follow Gustavo’s car – press Right Stick Click / Right Stick Click to lock onto it as it makes it easier to follow.

More enemies show up, in cars and on motorbikes this time. You can switch to Lucia if you’d like, who is hanging out of the sunroof with a gun, and defeat them.

Eventually, the car is t-boned and it rolls. If you were Lucia, it switches to Jason. Andrés is stuck in the upside-down car and two men on bikes appear – take them out.

Leave Andrés and get onto a bike. Lucia gets on the back. Continue chasing Gustavo.

You can switch to Lucia again to shoot pursuing enemies or control the bike as Jason. If you’re Jason, Lucia automatically fires so just focus on driving.

A chopper appears. If you’re Lucia, focus on its main propeller or tail rotor to take it down fast.

Andrés appears in another vehicle and sideswipes Gustavo’s car. It flips and ends up falling over a bridge and onto a train track. And a train is coming.

As Lucia, rush over to the car and press Triangle / Y on the passenger side door to get to Rafa.

He’s stuck – the seatbelt is jammed. Mash R2 / RT and Lucia cuts it with a knife.

He isn’t free yet, though, as his leg is jammed behind the front seat. Use the left thumbstick to find the sweet spot, then mash Circle / B to free him just in time.

Jason spots Gustavo trying to sneak off; he somehow escaped before the train smashed through the car. You switch to him.

Follow the marker to chase Gustavo down as he runs away. You find him collapsed on the side of the freeway a short distance away and you’re prompted to deal with him. If you hold L2 / LT , you can Question ( Cross / A ) or Threaten ( Square / X ) him multiple times for more dialogue.

You have two choices here: kill Gustavo or spare him while you wait for Andrés.

If you kill Gustavo, Andrés is impressed and there’s no consequence. If you spare him and wait for Andrés, he eventually reaches Jason and kills Gustavo himself.[/index.php?title=/wikis/gta-6/File:37.gta_6_childs_play_kill_gustavo.jpg%26action%3Dedit%26redlink%3D1 alt=37.gta 6 childs play kill gustavo.jpg]

Time fast forwards to the next day. Jason and Lucia are enjoying a meal with Andrés and Rafa before Petra arrives – she’s ecstatic to have her son back. Andrés takes most of the credit, of course.

Back at the Y Hotel, Valentina calls; Abe is ecstatic as he’s secured his contract with the Navarros off the back of Jason and Lucia’s hard work, which spells good news for potentially getting Tomás back.

The mission ends and Andrés transfers $30,000 via BuckMe as a thank you for rescuing Rafa.

Once Rafa has been rescued, Nate finally calls Lucia. Kordell Grant is planning the big job they keep talking about and wants the crew to meet up. This starts the Power Play main mission .

articles.title: Delivery Method Walkthrough - GTA 6 Guide - IGN
articles.summary: After discovering the details of Kordell Grant’s elaborate plan to hit the airport with his crew in Grand Theft Auto VI Chapter 4, Andrea asks Jason to
articles.body:
After discovering the details of Kordell Grant’s elaborate plan to hit the airport with his crew in Grand Theft Auto VI Chapter 4 , Andrea asks Jason to meet so they can set up a fake identity for Lucia as she goes undercover. This official IGN GTA 6 guide walks you through the Delivery Method main mission.

Andrea wants to set up a fake identity for Lucia as part of the heist. Meet her at the planning room.

When you’re ready to start the Delivery Method main mission, head back to Raul’s planning room as Jason.

Jason meets with Andrea, who reveals that the wine expert Lucia needs to pretend to be at the airport looks nothing like her. He’s worried.

There is something he can do, though: sneak into the Transport Security Services (TSS) offices as a phony food delivery driver, plug in a drive, and replace the expert’s fingerprints with Lucia’s in their database so she passes through security with no issues.

Jason gets on a bicycle, dressed as an unassuming Hotbox driver. Ride over to the security gate, which is 0.37 miles away. The GPS route is automatically marked for you.

Approach the gate. Jason is waved on through – nice and easy. Follow the marker for the TSS office entrance.

Enter the building, then highlight the receptionist with L2 / LT and press Cross/A to talk to her. Jason drops off the order and asks for the code for confirmation.

The receptionist calls up to inform the recipient their food is here, but there’s no answer. She rushes off on foot to find them.

Quickly move behind the desk and press Triangle / Y to hack the receptionist’s PC. Wait, then remove it with Triangle / Y again.

It didn’t work; Jason needs a computer with higher access clearance, likely in the main office on the second floor.

You need to cause an evacuation to buy Jason time to get up there and plug in the hack. You can either do this aggressively or take the stealth approach.

If you fail to hack the database, you won’t fail the mission. Instead, Lucia faces more security at the airport later down the line.

If you would rather take the stealthy approach rather than cause a scene, you can. You can do this in multiple ways, though the following way is how we did it.

Begin by finding the fire alarm. It’s on the right side of the receptionist’s desk, next to the filing cabinets. Approach and hold Triangle / Y to set it off.

The building evacuates. You have 90 seconds to pull off the hack before firefighters arrive.

Quickly head upstairs through the door to the right of the main entrance doors. Make sure to wait for all the employees to leave before you go up!

If you don’t wait for everyone to leave before going upstairs, the receptionist spots you. She asks you to evacuate. If you don’t, she calls the police and you get a 1-Star Wanted Level – oops.

Head through the Floor 2 door. Walk forward to the end of the room and look to the left to see a door with “Manager” on.

Go inside and hack the PC, then remove the drive when prompted.

Leave the building the way you came. If you take too long to exit, firefighters show up and kick you out of the building anyway.

If stealth isn’t your thing, you can take the aggressive approach. Here’s what we did. Once you are prompted to find the PC on the second floor, equip your gun. Walk upstairs through the door to the right of the main entrance doors.

Head through the Floor 2 door, then point your gun at the employees here. You can press Square / X to threaten them, if you’d like.

You need to hack the PC in the manager’s office. Walk forward to the back of the room, then look to the left to spot a “Manager” door. Head inside.

Point the gun at the manager and she falls to the floor, scared. Quickly hack her PC, wait for it to complete, then remove the drive.

You can destroy the office’s security footage, if you’d like. Leave the Manager office and go through the door directly ahead.

Inside, there’s a stack of machines; press Triangle / Y on them to destroy the CCTV video. This removes the camera icon from your Wanted bar.

At this point, the police will likely be on their way. You start with a 1-Star Wanted Level, but it can quickly move up to 2-Star if you’re not careful.

To make it out without being spotted, return to the stairs and head up to the roof. Climb down the back of the building and you can hop over the fence and make your getaway undetected.

If you leave out the front, you get into a police shootout, which raises your Wanted Level. You need to successfully clear your heat to progress.

It doesn’t matter how you get out of there, so do so however you see fit.

When you’re clear of the building, regardless of which approach you took, Jason texts the group chat informing them that he successfully hacked the database with Lucia’s information. The mission ends.

Depending on what you’ve completed so far, the following main missions may be available to you:

After Delivery Method is complete, Andrea texts: she wants Jason or Lucia to steal a catering truck. This adds the “Steal a Catering Truck” objective to your map, which starts the Fully Catered main mission .
