articles.body:
During GTA 6's Chapter 4 main mission Headliners , you'll need to pick who gets let into Club VYB. The VIPs you pick affects the revenue and number of impressions the club receives. You also get a different cutscene, depending on who you choose to let in, and you see them throughout the night.

When choosing which VIPs to let in, don’t just look at their monetary offer – their social media followers matter, too. Impressions also helps the club which, in turn, affects your payout at the end of the night.

In your decision, measure the VIPs’ offers against their social media followers. For example, Donatello offers nothing yet has almost 61 million followers; the impressions here are probably worth the risk.

We went with Donatello Lambrini , Game Developer , and Jimmy De Santa (an Easter Egg for GTA 5 fans!) for a total of $85,000 and 60,900,150 impressions

You can see the total value of your three selections in the top right corner of the screen. Once you’ve picked your three VIPs, hold Circle / B to confirm your choices .

Game Developer Offer: $50,000 Followers: 5,282

Donatello Lambrini Offer: $0 Followers: 60,839,593

Jimmy De Santa Offer: $35,000 Followers: 55,275

Later in the mission, Dre'Quan asks Jason to escort a special guest. When you go out a man approaches asking to be let in. If you let him in, it increases the revenue the club makes for the night, therefore increasing your cut of the profits.

articles.title: UFO Abduction Walkthrough - GTA 6 Guide - IGN
articles.summary: In Grand Theft Auto VI, you might come across a car that's acting funny. The lights will be flickering, the doors will be opened, and it will be emitting
articles.body:
In Grand Theft Auto VI , you might come across a car that's acting funny. The lights will be flickering, the doors will be opened, and it will be emitting some strange noises. This is the first stage of one of the biggest mysteries in Leonida in which Jason and Lucia encounter what could be an alien abduction. This official IGN GTA 6 walkthrough covers all the steps to completing this strange, optional mission. For completing it you will unlock Tap to Reveal

The Abandoned Car you need to find to begin this optional mission has a dynamic location, meaning it can appear in many areas, and at any point in the story. Also, it needs to be nighttime to find the car, as it will not spawn during the day – it only happens after 10 PM.

There are eight places where the Abandoned Car can spawn, with all eight being in the Kelly County region:

Head to any of the locations on the map above after 10 PM at night for a chance to encounter the Abandoned Car.

After finding one of the cars, use Focus Mode ( Left Stick Click + Right Stick Click / Left Stick Click + Right Stick Click ) to confirm for sure that it's the Abandoned Car you're looking for. If the car is glitching out and you see noise ripples coming from it in Focus, then you have found an Abandoned Car.

Approach to see a trail of clothing leading away from the car. As we mentioned, there are eight locations where this can happen, but the trail of clothes is typically in front of where the car is facing – where the headlights are shining.

It's best to pull out your flashlight from your inventory during this section, as it will likely be pitch black where you are. Using Focus Mode, continue to follow the trail of clothing items. The clothing items will be highlighted while in Focus Mode.

The trail of clothing items will eventually go cold, but once it does, you should be able to look ahead to see an incredibly bright blue and white light. If you still have your flashlight out, turn it off, as it helps you spot the light much better.

Also, you can activate Focus Mode here, and you should be able to see a ripple of sound coming from the bright light.

Once you see the light, start walking toward it. As you approach, you see a naked woman being abducted by what looks to be a giant UFO. It's hard to make out, as there's a blinding white light above you. Observe the abduction of the floating naked lady.

After a few moments, the lady drops to the ground, and the UFO takes off.

With the UFO gone, the naked lady is laying on the ground. Approach her and push the prompt to help her. As you do, she stands up and begins strangling you. After shoving the lady back to the ground, you can target her and ask if she is okay or tell her to snap out of it.

Eventually, she stands back up, comes back to her senses, and is very confused. At this point, target her again and select the choice to offer to help her. She asks you to go get her car.

Once the lady asks you to get her car, it will be marked with a pink dot on your minimap. Leave the lady and begin running to the car. Once you've made your way back to it, you'll notice that it has stopped glitching out. Attempt to enter the car, but once you do, a cutscene begins with your character being overcome with a mysterious light.

Once your character looks up to see where the light is coming from, they become completely engulfed by it and the screen goes dark. After a moment, your character wakes up on the ground, and it's daytime again. After some confusion, they stand up, and this section of the mission is over.

Depending on the state of your partner while you do this, you might receive a phone call from them saying they haven’t seen or heard from you for days. If you don't get the call, it's okay, it just means that for story reasons, your partner didn't call.

After Part 1 of the UFO Abduction optional mission is complete, continue playing. Eventually, after a few missions, you can try and sleep as the character (Jason or Lucia) who met the UFO previously.

Instead of going straight to sleep, your character begins to toss and turn, with flashbacks of the car and the woman. After a while, your character wakes up in a completely white room.

Right behind your character is a black wormhole-like void that you can run through. Once you get control, turn around and run into the wormhole to enter a black corridor of lights that opens into a giant room with alien eggs.

A cutscene plays, showing your character slowly approaching an egg, only to back off once it starts to hatch. Your goal here is to get through the egg field without disturbing them too much. If the egg turns blue, that means it's starting to hatch, and if it starts to glow yellow, that means it's about to crack open.

Across the way is a giant bright yellow light; that is where you need to go.

You want to make sure you crouch through this area. Walking normally, sprinting, or even crouch sprinting disturbs the eggs too much. If this happens, or you just get too close to one, the egg hatches and an alien tentacle springs out of the egg and grab your character. Don’t worry, though, as you’ll simply wake back up in the white room and be able to give the egg room another try.

If you fail again, a prompt to continue or give up appears. Continuing allows you to keep trying the egg room, while giving up sends you back to your safehouse.

Navigating the egg room is tricky because the corridors you pass through to not disturb the eggs are tight, but as long as you take it slow and don’t physically touch the egg, you should be okay.

The maps below show the safest route through the eggs.

After leaving the egg room, you find yourself in a very bright white room with another one of those wormholes, leading you into a room with the solar system. The globe where Earth should be (third from the left of the sun) is instead a fisheye view of Vice City.

Approach it to interact with it. What this globe is showing you is the mysterious location to trigger Stage 3 of this mission. You can spin the orb if you’d like to get a view of the surrounding area to see where you need to go but take note of the building with the big tower next to it.

Stop interacting with the orb to see a string of lights to the right. There is no puzzle involving the orb, as it is simply just showing you the next location that you need to find, so the moment you stop focusing on it, the lights to the right will trigger. Follow that string of lights to a keypad.

Above the keypad is a set of four lines, showing what the code is. We went through this sequence a few times, and the code always stayed the same: 2314 . It may vary for you, though.

After entering the keypad code and going through the door, you’ll find a control panel with an orange flashing light.

Approach the control panel and interact with it, then push the red button under the orange light. This causes the console panel to light up with a bunch of seemingly random lights.

You’ll then get to interact with four buttons on the control panel. The goal here is to make each of the lights blue. When pushing a button, it will cycle between blue and orange lights. Also, pushing one button will activate its light, plus the light to the left.

If the buttons are in the order of 1-2-3-4, with the far-left button being 1 and the far-right button being 4, you need to press them in this order:

If done correctly, the lever on the right turns blue, allowing you to pull it, which reveals three doors.

This is the final puzzle in this area, and luckily, it’s simple. After completing the control panel puzzle, three doors will appear. Do not go through the middle door. If you do, you find two giant globes, and your character starts taking damage immediately. If you do this too many times, your character dies, so avoid the middle door.

Instead, enter the door on the left to enter a giant white room. You’ll spot a small table. As you approach it, you’ll see cows on the left and right. Ignore them, approach the table, and grab the bottle of milk sitting on it.

While this will confuse the cows, causing them to begin walking toward you, ignore them and exit the room with the milk. Back in the room with three doors, enter the right door this time. You’ll once again be in a completely white room, with a small receptacle in the center. Approach it and deposit the milk bottle. Doing so causes your character to wake up. Your partner asks if you’re okay, to which your character describes the part of the dream where you saw the building and the tower while inspecting the globe. They tell their partner to let them know if they ever see it.

At this point, Part 2 of the UFO Abduction mission will end.

Part 3 of the UFO Abduction optional mission can be completed right after Part 2. In fact, you’ll learn that you didn’t even need Part 2 to be complete to do Part 3 – but skipping Part 2 means missing out on a very cool story moment, and some context and codes to complete Part 3. So, we’ll continue with the assumption that you have followed along thus far.

After completing Part 2, a prompt appears for you to find the Mysterious Location. There are no further clues as to where exactly this is, but depending on how much you explored in Chapter 1, you might already have an idea of where to go

Just north of Key Lento, when driving over the Shoeless Keys bridge heading toward Hamlet, you’ll spot the facility to the left of the bridge, just as it’s ending.

If you GPS to this spot on your map, it should bring you right up to the front gate.

As you approach the facility on the rocky road, surely enough, you’ll spot the small building with the giant tower to the right. This is exactly what was shown when inspecting the Earth globe in Stage 2. If you have a vehicle, go ahead and ram right through the gate – there won't be any police or people around, so there is no harm in doing this.

If you somehow got here without a vehicle, you’ll need to hop the fence, which you’ll see is covered in barbed wire. To do this, approach the fence and follow it around to the left, toward the big, broken-down satellite.

There’s a smaller tower in front of the satellite. Climb up the ladder to the tower, and get off after just one story.

Once up there, you’ll see a metal vent below, which follows the back side of the fence and eventually curves over it. Hop the railing and land on the vent. Slowly follow the vent forward and around the curve, which ends with you over the fence.

Now that you’re over, make your way back to the front of the building so we can give directions for whether you hopped the fence or rammed through the gate.

Back in front of the building, swing around to the right to spot a ladder and a double door. You can take either way to get into the building, as there is a vent on the roof that will drop you into an office that will be right inside the double doors. So, approach the double doors and kick them open.

There’s a dark staircase immediately to the left when entering the double doors. We recommend that you pull out your flashlight for this section, as it is about to get very dark.

Once you go down the stairs, you're met with a locked door with a keypad. If you completed Stage 2, then the keypad has a note with the code from the keypad you found there. If you didn’t do Stage 2, that's okay: the code is 2314 .

After entering the door, you’ll be in a small room with an elevator. Enter the elevator and take it down to the basement. You’ll exit into a green room. As you make your way through the door, it is pitch black, so, reminder: pull out your flashlight.

Make your way down the hall; it will eventually turn right, which leads to an open door. You’ll be inside another dark corridor.

Make your way down the hall, and it’ll appear to split to either the left or the right, but you’ll discover that you can only go left. Do so and go through the door to enter a very familiar room (if you completed Stage 2).

While not as clean as it was in your dream, you’ll quickly discover that you are once again in the control panel room that you solved while asleep. You can even see the three doors that open once you solve the control panel.

Also, as a little bonus, there’s a small desk with a tape recorder in front of the control panel. Playing the tape reveals that they have been running experiments on aliens, that they like raw cow milk, and that cow abductions have been happening across the state because of this.

Once again, approach the control panel and press the button on the right to activate the four buttons. While looking at the four buttons, the one on the very left will be button 1, with the one on the very right being button 4. The order to press them is the same as it was in the dream, and is as follows:

If done correctly, the doors light up. If you remember, the middle door is the one that hurts you. If you're curious, push open the middle door and shine your flashlight inside to see a bunch of dead bodies. Clearly some sort of accident happened here while feeding the alien, which is why you took damage here in your dream.

Enter the door to your left, but instead of lively cows in a clean room, you’ll see decrepit cows with cow skeletons in them, indicating it has been a while since this facility has been used. Grab the milk bottle and leave the room.

Enter the right door to find the receptacle. Insert the bottle of cow milk. The machine powers on and a cutscene triggers.

Escaping the Mysterious Facility (Spoilers)

We are now on the final part of the UFO Abduction mission! If you’d like to see how it all ends for yourself, you can click away now, or you can continue to follow this guide.

After the cutscene plays, it is revealed that there is in fact an actual alien inside the contraption. You can interact with it a couple of times, but the alien is non-responsive. Pick the alien up. Doing so causes the alarms to go off. You won’t be able to use your flashlight to escape, as you are now holding the alien, but luckily the lights from the alarm help guide your way. You can also use your minimap to guide your way out. After picking up the alien, start running down the hall to re-enter the control panel room. Continue left through the red, blinking hallway, following the green lights.

At the end of the hall, turn right and make your way down the halls to find the elevator. Call the elevator and use it to return to the first floor. Once the elevator opens back up, run straight up the stairs and approach the door – a cutscene plays.

The cutscene sees your character exiting the facility, and then is immediately blinded by the light from the UFO above. Your character looks down at the alien, who has now woken up, and is lifted into the UFO. After the alien reaches the UFO, it takes off, and you’ll get a bonus to your max Focus, Stamina, and Health.

You may think the mission is over, but there is one more surprise. As you begin to leave the area, you are quickly surrounded by men in dark SUVs, demanding that you freeze. After a few moments, the UFO shows back up and uses lasers to destroy all the vehicles.

Each vehicle explodes, and the UFO hovers there for a moment. Run over to the light and your character thanks the UFO, which once again flies away. After it does, the mission is finally over, and you are free to leave the area.

At this point, the UFO Abduction mission is now complete! As a reward, all three stats get a permanent, small increase, regardless of the stat level.

articles.title: A Skeleton Cyclops Collection Walkthrough - Enshrouded Guide - IGN
articles.summary: A Skeleton Cyclops Collection is a multi-part Enshrouded quest that sends you six different caves and one enemy base to track down all seven pieces of a
articles.body:
A Skeleton Cyclops Collection is a multi-part Enshrouded quest that sends you six different caves and one enemy base to track down all seven pieces of a cyclops skeleton. Once you have all the pieces, you can assemble one of the most impressive decorations in the game. If you're missing one or two pieces of the giant beast and you're not sure where to find them, you'll find everything you need in this Enshrouded guide .

The Cyclops Left Leg is found in the Cyclops Cave Passage near Bittermelt Lake. The easiest way to get there is to glide from the Balefire Tower "1000 Miles". Glide southwest off the tallest part of the tower and search the side of the mountain as you're gliding. Keep your eyes peeled for a cave entrance along the side of the rocky cliffs. Make your way inside the cave once you spot it, but prepare for a fight, because there is a massive cyclops waiting there for you.

Cyclops are massive enemies armed with giant clubs. They are not afraid to use them, either, so expect to dodge a lot of swings and hits from the huge weapon. Cyclops are also known to stomp with their feet, so if you're fighting up close, keep an eye on the beast's legs and dodge out of the way when you see it lift its great foot before slamming it back down. Cyclops are weak to Shroud damage, so if you have a weapon that inflicts it, that would be a good option here!

Defeat the giant foe and loot the body to collect the Cyclops Left Leg. Then, you're free to move on to the next cyclops challenge.

The Cyclops Right Leg is attached to a cyclops in a cave passage behind Everfore Keep in the Albaneve Summits. To get there, you first need to make your way to Everfore Keep. Fast travel to the Albaneve Summits Ancient Spire and soar off the northeastern side.

Drop down on the path, and start following it. You'll pass through an enshrouded area, the Gateway Outpost "Alba", the eventually find yourself in the Forge of Obsidia.

The Forge of Obsidia is actually the location of another quest, A Blast Furnace for the Blacksmith . Defeat enemies inside the main forge room until one of them drops the Bellows item. Tuck that away in your pack and use it to craft a Blast Furnace for the Blacksmith once you get back to your base!

For now, continue through the Forge by taking the doorway to the right and following that up a set of stairs. Turn left at the top of the stairs to get back outside again. Turn left as soon as you exit the building and continue following the path until you reach a dead-end.

Take a closer look at the cliff on your right to discover a cave entrance and a new path. Follow it until it branches and you can see some steel arches on the right. Take the path leading left, and continue following it to reach Evermore Keep.

Evermore Keep is locked up tight, so sneak around the traps to the locked door on the left and use a Lockpick to open it. Once you're in, head forward and go up the stairs to find yourself in a courtyard. Climb the stairs opposite and run up to a pile of rubble.

Turn left when you reach the rubble and follow the path around the side of the building to reach a grate. Climb the grate and run up the stairs on the left. Work your way around the grounds until you reach a courtyard with stairs leading up the left and right. Run straight up any set of steps and continue north until you reach a dead-end.

Glide off the ledge to reach the enshrouded portion of the building. Head forward into the ruined hall, and climb the stairs on the right to find yourself back outside again. Run straight ahead and turn right at the corner of the building to find a wagon with a grate on the wall beside it.

Climb the grate to find yourself in near a small garden. Head east and look up to your left to spot two grapple points.

These will bring you back out of the shroud. Take the stairs on the northern side of the room, run forward to get back outside, turn right, and right again to reach a large courtyard. Take the stairs on the left and follow them to another courtyard containing a well.

Hook around to your right to climb another small staircase, turn left, and climb the next set. Turn left again to find a large stone archway leading out of Evermore Keep, and follow the road heading northeast. You'll eventually come across a large drop.

Jump and use your grapple hook to swing forward then quickly grab the next grapple point to pull yourself up to the other side. Climb the grate on the left, and continue pushing on.

This leads you to a small cavern on your left and a stack of rubble on your right. Climb the rubble to reach a grapple point on the left. Use that, then turn around and use the second grapple hook to your right. Finally, follow the road to the cyclops cave near the bridge.

There is, of course, a cyclops waiting for you at the end. Defeat it to retrieve the Right Cyclops Leg and get one step closer to finishing A Skeleton Cyclops Collection !

The Cyclops Right Arm can be found in the Cyclops Cave Passage just below Everfore Keep. To get there, glide off the northeastern side of the Albaneve Summits Ancient Spire and follow the road until you reach the Shroud.

Once you run past a small staircase leading up to your left, take it. The stairs lead to a broken pathway, so once you run out of path, jump down to the ice below and start heading northwest to reach the other side of the frozen lake.

There, you will find a small path that leads you right to the entrance to a cave passage. Inside, is the cyclops that holds the Cyclops Right Arm. Defeat it to claim your prize and move on to your next victim. Cyclops Right Arm

The Cyclops Torso is deep in an Albaneve Summits Elixir Well, and it's one of the toughest to track down. You will find it as you're completing the Ignite the Coldest Elixir Well quest.

The Elixir Well you're looking for is hidden deep in the Shroud just north of the Albaneve Summits tower. To reach it, fast travel to the Albaneve Summits Ancient Spire and jump off the northeastern side to the path below. Start following the path until you reach the Shroud.

Follow the path until it branches, then take the path leading left . Continue following the path once it branches, and you will eventually find yourself at a large, stone bridge. Make your way over the bridge and continue down the path to reach a large stone building that marks the entrance to the Elixir Well.

You will be met with enemies as soon as you reach the Elixir Well entrance. You can either take the time to knock each and every one of them out or just ignore them if you're concerned about running out of time in the Shroud.

Keep heading straight forward through the stone tunnel, keeping your eyes on the ground as you go. There's a hole in the ground about halfway down the hall with a chest inside, so pick that up before continuing on.

Eventually, you will find yourself at a dead end. Glide off the edge of the path and head straight forward, over some wooden structures and under some large, stone archways. Once you reach land on the other side, you will spot the first Shroud Root, along with a horde of enemies. Pick off the enemies around you to clear your way to the Shroud Root and start cutting it down with an axe. With the first Shroud Root taken care of, you'll be free to move on to the next one.

Make your way west to find a wooden platform leading to an air current. Glide off the edge and use the current to fly straight toward the second Shroud Root. Clear the surrounding bugs, cut that Shroud Root down, and turn east to spot a grapple point in the distance. Use your Grapple Hook to reach the upper level and head straight toward the third Shroud Root.

You will get a Fell Cyclops Head for defeating the monster, which you can use to upgrade your flame, a Shroud Nexus, some other items, and a Cyclops Torso piece, which you can use to complete the A Skeleton Cyclops Collection quest for the Collector.

The Cyclops Pelvis you need for A Skeleton Cyclops Collection is currently attached to a cyclops in a cave near Polaris Falls in the northern part of the Albaneve Summits. To get there, glide off the northwestern side of the Albaneve Summits Ancient Spire and follow the road until you pass Lake Luma on your left.

Continue following the road past Lake Luma and push forward until you reach Polaris Falls . Turn right from the main entrance to see another path hugging the cliff leading south. Climb up there and keep following that road until you reach the Cyclops Cave.

Head in there to face off against yet another cyclops, and don't forget to pick up his Pelvis before you go! That puts you one step closer to completing A Skeleton Cyclops Collection for the Collector.

You will find the Cyclops Left Arm in the Quiet Caves in the Wildwater Basin. To get there, fast travel to the Albaneve Summits Ancient Spire and soar off the northeastern side.

Glide straight forward until you start to approach two windcurrents. Hitch a ride on the currents to the land straight ahead and turn left. Follow that road until you reach the Wildwater Basin. The Quite Caves are along the western side of the Basin, but beware! There is a cyclops waiting for you there. Defeat it to collect the next piece of your cyclops puzzle.

The Cyclops Skull is hidden in a small room in Balefire Stronghold "Lance Point", and it's the only piece of the cyclops puzzle that you don't have to fight for. The easiest way to get the the Balefire Stronghold "Lance Point" is to travel up the mountain from the Wildwater Basin, or soar off Howling Peak, fly around the side of the mountain, and drop down to the base.

The base is split into two sections, one of which has a collection of buildings and the other, found on the opposite side of a massive crevasse, has the balefire. The Cyclops Skull is inside the large tower bordering the crevasse opposite the balefire tower.

Once you have all seven pieces of the cyclops, you just need to assemble them! For that, you will need a Cyclops Showcase which you can craft with the Collector . To make one, you'll need the following materials, most of which can be found in the Hollow Halls:

15x Metal Sheets: Can be crafted at the Forge using 2x Metal Scraps and 2x Charcoal.

15x Charcoal: Process Wood Logs and Dirt in the Charcoal Kiln.

10x Ectoplasm Blocks: Recipe can be found in a chest in the Nomad Highlands Hollow Halls.

5x Ectoplasm Fragment: Mined and found in Hollow Halls dungeons.

Once you've got your Cyclops Showcase, place it in an area with a very high roof, and interact with it to select your cyclops pieces. Place each part in the appropriate slot to build the Skeleton Cyclops display and complete A Skeleton Cyclops Collection !

For more helpful Enshrouded tips and guides, check out the following pages:

Up Next: The Albaneve Summits Hollow Halls

articles.title: GTA 6 Analysis Shows PS5 Version Suffers 'Substantially' More Frequent Frame Rate Drops Than Xbox Series X Version, Sparking Debate About Sony's 'Plays Best on PS5' Marketing
articles.summary: The tech experts at Digital Foundry have revealed their analysis of GTA 6, and found the game performs “meaningfully better” on Xbox Series X than the base PS5.
articles.body:
The tech experts at Digital Foundry have revealed their analysis of GTA 6 , and found the game performs “meaningfully better” on Xbox Series X than the base PS5.

Sony’s high-profile marketing deal for GTA 6 involved the key phrase, “Plays Best on PS5,” and while that marketing tagline encompasses more than just performance, many are now questioning its validity with GTA 6 out in the wild.

Digital Foundry found that Xbox Series X provides a “virtually identical visual presentation” to the PS5 in terms of overall image clarity and presentation quality, but there is a significant split on performance.

As Rockstar had announced before launch, GTA 6 “targets” 30 frames per second across all platforms, from the Xbox Series S up to the PS5 Pro, but there are moments where the frame rate drops. According to DF’s analysis , the frame rate suffers more on PS5 than Series X.

PS5 suffers substantially more frequent frame-rate drops than Series X, which is compounded by the fact that the Xbox machine also benefits from 120Hz VRR support to smooth out minor dips. Ultimately, Series X is meaningfully better off.

Of course, the PS5 Pro version offers the best experience in terms of performance, but it’s interesting to see the Xbox Series X outperform the PS5 here. Some are pointing to non-performance related features, such as the PS5’s haptic feedback, which is great for driving, as playing a role in the phrase “Plays Best on PS5,” and we should be used to marketing speak that is technically not wrong by now. But, as DF reveals, when it comes to performance, there can be no doubting the clear winner.

Indeed, some are calling the “Plays Best on PS5,” phrase “grossly misleading,” claiming that Sony should have said “Plays Best on PS5 Pro” instead.

“I’ve been f***ing fooled,” one person said in the comments of DF’s YouTube video . “They did kind of say in the fine print that ‘best’ referred to the features in the DualSense controller,” another person countered.

“If you are advertising ‘Plays best on X’ to gamers, the immediate thought is going to be ‘Out the two places I can play the game, it is going to play the best on the X console,’” another suggested. “What does ‘Play’ mean to that audience? Performance, stability, possibly higher resolution, less texture pop-in.”

In June, when Sony trumpeted the “Plays Best on PS5” marketing line , it highlighted how GTA 6 takes advantage of the PS5 DualSense controller's haptic feedback and integrated speaker. Sony also highlighted its Tempest 3D AudioTech, which allows you to "surround yourself in the distinct soundscapes of Leonida" through its "highly accurate audio positioning." GTA 6 would also "leverage the PS5's ultra-high speed SSD" to experience GTA 6 "with near-instant load times." Sony's blog post made no mention of performance.

Meanwhile, there are questions around GTA 6’s use of FSR 4.1 on the Xbox Series S version of the game only . Rather than rendering the game at the console's native 1440p, Rockstar used AMD's FSR 4.1 to upscale from 720p to 1080p, which makes GTA 6 one of the first games to use the new upscaling tech on Xbox. It’s thought this tech is what made GTA 6 possible at 30fps on the underpowered Series S in the first place.

Both the Xbox Series X and base PS5 versions of the game instead use Rockstar's in-house TAA (temporal anti-aliasing) solution, and the PS5 Pro uses Sony’s PSSR upscaler. But why not use FSR 4.1 on the Xbox Series X version of GTA 6 also? Similarly, if the PS5 version already supports PSSR, why not use Sony’s AI upscaling model QSSR (Quick Spectral Super Resolution)?

Elsewhere, fans are just marveling at the performance of GTA 6 on Xbox Series S, which — as we’ve reported — shows what Microsoft’s cheaper console is capable of. Ultimately, DF is hoping Rockstar releases GTA 6 updates that improve performance across the board, potentially adding 120Hz VRR support on PlayStation hardware and “stabilising” base console frame rates.

Just getting started in GTA 6 or wondering what to do next? Check out the Official Grand Theft Auto 6 guide right here on IGN. If you're still getting your bearings, discover GTA's new systems with the Beginner's Guide - 67 Tips and Tricks , or get all the details on the first chapters with the Chapter 1 Guide and Tips , Chapter 2 Guide and Tips , and Chapter 3 Guide and Tips . If you're already driving all around Leonida and want to know everything there is to find and do, see the Leonida interactive map .

Wesley is IGN's Managing Editor. Find him on Twitter at @wyp100. You can reach Wesley at wesley_yinpoole@ign.com or confidentially at wyp100@proton.me.
